lines.japanese: 自分が普通じゃないってことに気付いたのはいつ頃だったろう。
lines.english: When did I first realize I wasn't normal?

lines.japanese: 誰にだってあるよね。自分にとっては当たり前だと思っていたことが、一般的にはそうでもなかったんだって気付く、そういう経験。
lines.english: It happens to everyone, doesn't it? One day you discover that something you've always taken for normal isn't normal at all.

lines.japanese: 自分のことを「ぼく」と呼ぶのが子供たちの間では格好悪いことだとか、一度もリフォームしないまま築３０年を越しているうちの家が、周囲の景観からわりと浮きあがってることだとか──
lines.english: Maybe you discover that the other kids think the way you talk about yourself sounds lame. Or that your house, over thirty years old and never once remodeled, looks rather out of place in the neighborhood—

lines.japanese: ──もう覚えてないけれど、いつか昔に気が付いたんだろう。
lines.english: —I don't remember anymore. I must have noticed sometime, long ago.

lines.japanese: だったら、他の子は誰も、向こうの世界に呼ばれたりしないんだって気付いたのはいつ頃だったろう。
lines.english: And when did I realize that none of the other children were ever called to that other world?

lines.japanese: そのことをひとに言っても信じてもらえないばかりか、頭のおかしな子としか思われないんだって気付いたのはいつ頃だったろう。
lines.english: When did I realize that if I told anyone, not only would they refuse to believe me, they would simply think I was a crazy child?

lines.japanese: だから僕は、いま初めて僕以外の誰かにこんな話が出来て、少しばかりほっとしているんだ。
lines.english: So now that I can finally tell someone—anyone but myself—I'm a little relieved.

lines.japanese: 僕にとって言葉を持たない君は、ちょうど王様の耳を見てしまった理髪師が地面に掘った穴──
lines.english: To me, voiceless as you are, you're just like the hole King Midas's barber dug after seeing the king's ears—

lines.japanese: ──あ、ごめん、そんな風に言ったら気を悪くしちゃうかな。
lines.english: —Oh. Sorry. Maybe that was insulting.

lines.japanese: はじめまして、見知らぬ方。次元の狭間へようこそ。
lines.english: A pleasure to meet you, stranger. Welcome to the space between dimensions.

lines.japanese: 僕の名前は羽田鷹志。私立美空学園の三年生。
lines.english: My name is Takashi Haneda. I'm a third-year at the private Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: せっかく出会えたのに残念だけど、僕はもう何日かしたら、僕の魂が生まれた世界へ帰らなければならないんだ。なぜって、この逃避行は最初から期限付きの旅だったんだから。
lines.english: It's a shame, when we've only just met, but in a few days I have to return to the world where my soul was born. This flight of mine always had a time limit.

lines.japanese: いずれ分かることだから先に打ちあけてしまうと、いまの僕──つまり羽田鷹志は、グレタガルドの先代国王が集めた次期王候補“万色の四枚羽根”のひとり、聖騎士ホークの≪転生≫した姿だ。
lines.english: You'll find out eventually, so I may as well tell you now. The present me—Takashi Haneda—is the reincarnation of Holy Knight Hawk, one of the Four Wings of Many Colors, whom Gretagard's former king gathered as candidates to succeed him.

lines.japanese: うん。いいよ、笑ってくれて。慣れてるんだ、そういう目には。
lines.english: Yes. Go ahead and laugh. I'm used to that look.

lines.japanese: じゃあ、勝手に話を続ける。
lines.english: I'll go on, then.

lines.japanese: 翼人兵の凄惨な侵攻の果て、グレタガルドが陥落した折、次期王候補たる四人は死の際に立たされた。
lines.english: When Gretagard fell at the end of the Winged Soldiers' brutal invasion, the four candidates for the next king stood on the brink of death.

lines.japanese: 選択肢はふたつあった。非業の憤死を遂げ、グレタガルドの大地に眠るか。忌まわしい妖しの秘術にすがり、はるか異界の赤子として第二の生を得るか。
lines.english: There were two choices. Die bitter, untimely deaths and sleep beneath the soil of Gretagard. Or cling to a vile and uncanny secret art, and be granted second lives as infants in a faraway world.

lines.japanese: 僕らは≪転生≫の道を選んだ。
lines.english: We chose the path of reincarnation.

lines.japanese: 逃げるためじゃない。戦うためだ。別れのとき僕らは誓った。いつかまた故郷の地につどい、グレタガルドの王旗を掲げようと。
lines.english: Not to run away. To fight. As we parted, we swore that one day we would gather again in our homeland and raise the royal banner of Gretagard.

lines.japanese: そして時が流れ、君が僕を迎えに来た。
lines.english: Then time passed, and you came to take me home.

lines.japanese: ああ、大丈夫。安心していいよ。僕みたいな境遇のひとの中には、かりそめの世界に必要以上の愛着が涌いちゃって、未練がましく残留を主張するケースもあるんじゃないかと思う。
lines.english: Yeah, it’s okay. Don’t worry. I guess some people in my situation get way too attached to this temporary world and start insisting on staying because they can’t let go.

lines.japanese: だけど僕には、そんな未練も愛着も全然ないから。
lines.english: But I have no such regrets or attachments. None at all.

lines.japanese: すごいよね。呆れるぐらいにないんだ。あとを濁す心配いらずの、意味がない空っぽな１８年間。
lines.english: Pretty amazing, right? There’s so little even I can’t believe it. Eighteen empty, meaningless years, with no mess to leave behind.

lines.japanese: あるとき僕は携帯電話のメモ帳を開いた。
lines.english: One day, I opened the memo pad on my phone.

lines.japanese: むかし観た映画に、癌の宣告をされたヒロインが命尽きるまでに果たしたい事柄を紙面へ書きだしてゆくってシーンがあったから、それに倣ってみようと思ったんだ。
lines.english: There was a scene in a film I'd seen once: a heroine, told she had cancer, writing down all the things she wanted to do before her life ran out. I decided to follow her example.

lines.japanese: だけど一行目に“残務処理”という見出しを打ってからは、なかなか手が進まなかった。この世界から消える前にやっておきたいこと、っていうのがすぐに思いうかばなかった。
lines.english: But once I'd typed “Unfinished Business” at the top, my fingers stalled. I couldn't think of anything I wanted to do before I disappeared from this world.

lines.japanese: 法や倫理を超えた夢見事ならいくらでも思いつくんだけど（銀行強盗とか学園爆破とか性にまつわるエトセトラとか）、あとに残される家族のことを思うと犯罪行為・非人道的行為は慎みたい。
lines.english: Outside the bounds of law and morality, ideas came easily enough—rob a bank, blow up the school, indulge in assorted sexual escapades—but when I thought of the family I'd leave behind, crime and inhumanity seemed best avoided.

lines.japanese: かと言って現実的な範囲で考えれば、経済的な理由や能力的な問題でおのずと行動は制限される。
lines.english: Once I limited myself to realistic choices, though, money and ability fenced me in.

lines.japanese: 僕はしばらく悩んだ末、のろのろと“上杉家で『信長の野心』をクリアする”と打った。あれはとても面白いゲームだけど、時間がかかるからそれなりに気合を入れないと最後までやり通せないんだ。
lines.english: After thinking it over for a while, I slowly typed, “Beat *Nobunaga’s Ambitions* as the Uesugi clan.” It was a great game, but finishing it took time and a fair bit of determination.

lines.japanese: そして次に“学食のチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食を食べる”と入れた。すぐ売りきれてしまう、学園一の人気メニュー。どうせなら一度くらい味わっておきたい。
lines.english: Next came, “Eat the cafeteria’s sautéed chicken and fried shrimp meal.” It was the most popular meal at school and sold out almost immediately. I wanted to taste it at least once.

lines.japanese: さて志の低い文字列がふたつ続いたので、もうちょっとアカデミックな目標でも立てようと思って三つめに打ちこんだのが“期末テストで平均７０点以上とる”だ。
lines.english: With two such unambitious entries in a row, I decided my third ought to be a little more academic: “Average at least seventy on the final exams.”

lines.japanese: 五段階評価でいうところのＡやＢではなく、さりとてＣでもＤでもない、いうなればＢとＣの中間あたりにハードルを設ける小ざかしさが我ながら僕らしい。
lines.english: On a five-tier grading scale, I had set the bar not at an A or B, but not quite down at C or D either: neatly between B and C. That petty little calculation was entirely like me.

lines.japanese: でも、そのあと四つめ以降の項目が続かず、そのうちに眠くなってきて僕はケータイを閉じた。
lines.english: But no fourth item followed, let alone anything after it. Eventually I grew sleepy and closed my phone.

lines.japanese: つまりは僕の人生なんてその程度。趣味も生き甲斐も何もない。目標を果たすどころか、目標を立てることすらままならない。
lines.english: That was the measure of my life. No hobbies. Nothing to live for. I couldn't even set myself a goal, never mind accomplish one.

lines.japanese: いいんだけどね。
lines.english: Which was fine.

lines.japanese: だって、もともと虚しい思いをしないで済むようにって、そのために僕は、いつだって努めて世界の隅っこを歩いてきたんだから。
lines.english: I mean, I’d always gone out of my way to walk at the very edge of the world so I wouldn’t have to feel empty in the first place.

lines.japanese: うん、まあ……。
lines.english: Well… more or less.

lines.japanese: まったくないかって言われると、そうだな、ちょっとぐらいは……あるかもしれないけど。未練。
lines.english: If you asked whether there was truly nothing, I suppose… there might be a little. Perhaps a little lingering attachment.

lines.japanese: 胸に残しておきたい想い出。
lines.english: Memories I wanted to keep in my heart.

lines.japanese: 優しかったおじいさん。
lines.english: The kind old man.

lines.japanese: 可愛がってくれた叔父さん、叔母さん。
lines.english: My aunt and uncle, who'd always been so good to me.

lines.japanese: あまり仲良くはなかったかもしれないけど、大切な妹だった小鳩。
lines.english: Kobato, my precious little sister, even if perhaps we were never especially close.

lines.japanese: たったひとりの友達だった森里君。
lines.english: Morisato, the only friend I ever had.

lines.japanese: それと、もうひとつの誰にも明かしてない秘密。
lines.english: And one other secret I've never shared with anyone.

lines.japanese: 僕の初恋のひと。
lines.english: My first love.

lines.japanese: なんて、あはは、もうすぐそれも終わりだけどね。
lines.english: Well... ha-ha. That will be over soon, too.

lines.japanese: そうして僕は気持ちひとつ抱えず、近所の公園でも行くみたいにふらりと消えてしまおう。
lines.english: Then I can slip away with no feelings left to carry, as casually as if I were strolling down to the neighborhood park.

lines.japanese: 不器用な心に厳しかったこの世界から。
lines.english: Out of a world that never had much mercy for a clumsy heart.

lines.japanese: だけど、まだその時は来ない。
lines.english: But that time hasn't come yet.

lines.japanese: あともう少しだけ、僕の空っぽな物語は続くんだ。
lines.english: My empty story will go on a little longer.

lines.japanese: （ちなみに“残務処理”のひとつめは先日めでたく完遂した）
lines.english: (Incidentally, I successfully completed the first item on my “Unfinished Business” list the other day.)
